entries.defect: Treat the written inventory as observed evidence, distinguish inferred causes, and record that pictures, the truncated mask tail and the omitted pipeline/runtime files were unavailable for this analysis.
Replace the universal swept-outline construction with body-derived fitted regions, sewn deformable panels and anatomically attached rigid accessories within one pipeline.
Establish garment correspondence against the body actually rendered, preserving its topology mapping, morphs and anatomical boundaries rather than fitting only the full-resolution source.
Finalize and normalize the exported four skin influences before any inverse posing or fit evaluation so construction and runtime use the same deformation.
Build trousers with a connected seat, crotch and separate leg branches, removing the overlapping seat-and-leg tube construction.
Make fitted garment regions the visible replacement for their covered body faces, with shared anatomical deformation and deliberate garment ease rather than two competing surfaces.
Join shirt and robe sleeves to authored armholes and yokes, preserving shoulder and clavicle deformation instead of cutting intersecting sleeve triangles.
Give necklines, cuffs and trouser hems finished boundaries and retained interior skin continuations; keep duplicated seam positions, weights and morphs identical.
Construct breast cloths as tensioned front panels with fitted side, back and lower edges, removing the flange without copying the breast anatomy into a painted-on garment.
Treat the current knee-length shirt’s hanging lower section as loose cloth while retaining a fitted upper body and sleeves.
Build loin flaps and aprons from fitted waistbands and independent front/back panels that move against the thighs and buttocks rather than hang rigidly or average both legs.
Preserve the recognizable girdle-tail design while giving its attachments and free tails the same explicit construction contract.
Fit children’s short skirts to child pelvis and buttock shapes with modest drape, eliminating the all-round box without converting skirts into shorts or tight body paint.
Construct knee skirts, long wraps and robe skirts from sewn panels with controlled gathers and intentional hems instead of one convex envelope around both legs.
Give waist and chest wraps real overlapping edges and body-specific attachment fits; use only garment-appropriate openings and preserve overlap through motion.
Construct each toga’s supported shoulder, diagonal edge and lower panels explicitly, retaining left/right wearing differences while removing the inflated lower bag.
Remove circumferential skirt-weight blurring and the automatic transfer of shin, foot and toe weights to thighs.
Add small cloth control meshes with attachment, stretch, bend and contact constraints for free panels, driven after the complete runtime body pose is known.
Evaluate garment attachments and collisions after clip blending, stride changes, lean, clavicle motion, gaze and IK; verify the exact ordering against the omitted implementation.
Maintain complete collision bodies independently of rendered body masks, using efficient anatomical proxies and more accurate surfaces where needed.
Handle swept limb motion and panel face/edge contacts as well as vertex contacts so fast limbs and large triangles cannot bypass collision handling.
Include ground contact and controlled gathering for kneeling and digging so long hems do not become horizontal rings or pass through the ground.
Preserve panel overlap order and resolve relevant cloth self-contact, especially wrap seams and folded skirt regions.
Embed loose render surfaces in solved control-mesh frames, preserve exact fitted-to-loose seam positions and avoid applying skeletal deformation twice.
Reconstruct cloth normals from the final deformation and verify both backends’ position and shading results.
Use strongly damped constrained drape as the baseline, with posed initialization and robust handling of spawning, teleportation, pauses and animation transitions.
Build capes and cloaks from shoulder supports, closures and hanging panels rather than an inflated hull enclosing the arms.
Give arms intentional routes beneath movable panels or through appropriate openings, and never conceal escaping hands or forearms to simulate correct cloth.
Fit one-shoulder cape edges and sash sections to their supports to remove shoulder bunching, waist loops and folding into the torso.
Shape chest capes and cloaks to span the torso naturally without a flared collar or transferred breast bulges, preserving required coverage during arm motion.
Replace global slot-based layer ordering with explicit acyclic relationships for actual co-worn garment regions, including hood/cloak, sling/cloak and apron/loin-flap pairs.
Fit only combinations the generator can actually produce, preventing nonexistent pairings from inflating otherwise valid garments.
Derive safe body and inner-garment omissions from explicit regions and supported motion, retaining all surfaces visible through moving openings.
Replace per-vertex hide-bit union with face-safe coverage decisions so different garments cannot accidentally delete an uncovered triangle together.
Remove the universal inward-normal garment push as a repair mechanism; resolve visible interfaces with fitted geometry, overlap and contact.
Preserve the required seasonal inner garments under Zulu, Tuareg and Hausa wraps while masking safely concealed regions and fitting exposed interfaces.
Enforce the everyday open-outer no-inner-top rule together with women’s upper-body coverage, rejecting only wearing arrangements that cannot satisfy both.
Preserve children’s hip coverage through all supported poses and do not remove required dress layers merely because an outer garment usually hides them.
Separate hood head support from its neck transition and shoulder drape, with explicit overlap against robes, togas and cloaks.
Fit the veil’s head section and flexible lower collar overlap separately, checking head turns and clavicle extremes without masking away the neck indiscriminately.
Diagnose the veil’s dark neck band and uniform dark head using actual geometry, material and lighting views before choosing a readability correction.
Replace defective chest bead shells with deliberately arranged beadwork while preserving opaque upper-body coverage in Zulu youth and Mongo women’s outfits.
Do not replace covering chest beadwork with sparse necklaces unless an authorized same-people garment preserves the dress rule; the supplied excerpts do not establish such a replacement.
Fit neck and waist bead paths to each body and actual wearing layer, preserving bead shape and eliminating detached loops and tilted hip gaps.
Attach wrist rings rigidly to forearms and ankle rings rigidly to shins, orient them around limb axes and size them per body instead of blending across joints.
Retain cap, head-ring, topknot, hair-bag, headband and turban designs unless new evidence requires changes, while verifying morph fit and hood interactions.
Construct the baby sling as supported cloth and an exterior pouch with an identifiable infant attached to an upper-torso carrier frame, explicitly fitting its relationship to the cloak.
Fit garments to the actual supported sex, age and build combinations, including combined build extremes, instead of assuming adult-male offsets or ten isolated corners generalize.
Export explicit attachment, control-mesh, render-binding and coverage metadata with a versioned schema, keeping logical garment identity separate from render partitions and fit variants.
Verify that geometry morphing, joint adjustment and garment deformation follow the same runtime contract, with exact seam and attachment agreement after export.
Derive supported outfit relationships from the actual generator’s branches and boundaries, retaining all 158 inventory cases without assuming sampled random picks prove exhaustive coverage.
Restrict only unsupported or contradictory garment arrangements; retain seasonal layering, cultural distinctions and ordinary walking, running, kneeling and digging.
Share immutable topology and cache outfit coverage while keeping mutable cloth state per person, avoiding cross-person geometry or mask contamination.
Budget approximately 40–120 control vertices for small panels and 100–300 for major loose pieces, then measure solver, memory, vertex and draw costs in representative crowds.

Start with hundreds of render triangles for small garments and roughly 600–2,000 for substantial loose pieces, concentrating topology at seams, joints and contact regions rather than uniformly refining.
Group compatible material parts so beads, rings and fitted/loose partitions do not unnecessarily multiply draw calls; verify actual costs on WebGPU and WebGL 2.
Keep necessary coverage and contact correction functional at every quality level, and validate distance/update simplification without visible popping or stale cloth states.
Cache garment templates, body fits, deformation bindings and outfit coverage by their real inputs, measuring build time instead of assuming the replacement is faster.
Retire worst-pose rest inflation, repeated body/layer settling and automatic armhole deletion as the production garment construction path.
Retire capped-volume classification and tolerance-driven hide/push repair as production coverage logic, retaining geometric helpers only where independently useful.
Remove numeric penetration acceptance failures and stale gate documentation while retaining reports as diagnostics and structural failures for invalid or missing assets.
Cut over constructors, export schema, runtime consumers and generated asset together, removing obsolete configuration, cache dependencies and selectable legacy garment behavior.
Preserve MakeHuman source generation, anatomical skeleton and existing animation assets unless inspection identifies a specific incompatibility requiring change.
Track expected replacement risks explicitly: tight-joint pinching, painted-on shapes, seam cracks, stiff drape, jitter, stretching, overlap inversion, contact tunneling and shading artifacts.
Force walking trouser wearers into side-on port and village shots to reproduce the unresolved bare-thigh report instead of treating clean pipeline sheets as closure.
Re-shoot the child short-skirt diaper case and flap cases through full walk/run cycles, then verify kneeling, digging and transitions at normal viewing distances.
Visually check all recorded outfits plus newly discovered generator combinations across body builds, required motions, shoulder extremes, both backends and representative lighting.
Trace mesh ownership, masks and transforms for the hovering Bambara figure, detached fragments and Hausa spots before assigning a garment-specific fix.
Record before/after picture references and remaining defects per garment and outfit; accept the rebuild by moving in-game pictures rather than penetration values.
Update the implementation record and any documented dress deviations to match the final supported wearing arrangements without inventing seasonal or foreign garments.
